item.title: AnyLanguageModel adds on‑device speech and decision packages for Swift
item.description:
AnyLanguageModel adds on‑device speech and decision packages for Swift

Today the AnyLanguageModel project announced two new Swift packages — AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel — that extend its 1.x Swift API approach to speech transcription and decision‑making while keeping a familiar Apple‑style API.

🔍 Overview

  • AnySpeechRecognizer implements Apple’s new SpeechAnalyzer API but lets you pick the underlying engine, including NVIDIA’s Parakeet and Alibaba’s Qwen3‑ASR running locally via Core ML.
  • It adds speaker diarization to track who is speaking when.
  • AnyDecisionModel answers yes‑or‑no, multiple‑choice, and rating‑scale questions, returning typed results and probabilities derived from model logits rather than generated text.
  • Both packages can download open models from the Hugging Face Hub and run them entirely on‑device.

🗣️ AnySpeechRecognizer

  • Mirrors Apple’s SpeechAnalyzer, SpeechTranscriber, DictationTranscriber, SpeechDetector, and AssetInventory components.
  • Uses Apple’s Speech framework as the default engine; swapping to a different engine only requires changing the import.
  • Supports file‑based and live audio input, volatile results, word timing, and confidence scores when the selected engine provides them.
  • Includes built‑in speaker diarization.

🤖 AnyDecisionModel

  • Provides typed answers (yes/no, multiple‑choice, rating‑scale) with associated probabilities.
  • Derives answers from model probabilities, not from text generation.
  • Runs on‑device with MLX, Core AI, llama.cpp, or a decision model from Jev or Ollama.
  • Can be integrated with the same Swift API style used for language and speech models.

📦 Model Options

Model Size(s) Languages / Dialects Notable Traits
Parakeet v3 (NVIDIA) 0.6 B 25 European languages (auto‑detect locale) Runs on Core ML runtime, supports file & live input, volatile results, word timing, confidence
Parakeet Ultra (Moondream) 0.6 B (post‑trained) Same as v3 More accurate in most measurements
Parakeet Unified (NVIDIA) – English only –
Qwen3‑ASR (Alibaba) 0.6 B, 1.7 B 30 languages + 22 Chinese dialects (Mandarin, Cantonese, Japanese, Korean) Provides a single final result per ≤40 s segment, no volatile results, no word timing or confidence, runs on GPU, slower than Parakeet, better for file transcription

⚙️ How it works

  • You create a SpeechAnalyzer (or AnySpeechRecognizer) and attach modules such as SpeechTranscriber and SpeechDetector.
  • Provide an audio file or a stream of audio buffers; results are delivered via asynchronous sequences as they become available.
  • AssetInventory handles model installation; downloads occur only when the app requests them.
  • Models are stored in the standard Hugging Face cache, allowing a macOS app outside the sandbox to share them with Python or other Hugging Face tools.

🚀 Availability

  • Packages are available as Swift packages; they depend on the 1.x releases of AnyLanguageModel and swift‑huggingface.
  • Approximate download sizes (per model):
    • Parakeet variants: ~600 MB each + ~590 MB for the live encoder.
    • Qwen3‑ASR: 0.9 GB to 2.4 GB depending on model size.
    • Sortformer (used for speaker diarization): ~250 MB.
  • Once downloaded, models run entirely on‑device, with no ongoing cloud usage required.

#Swift #SpeechRecognition #OnDeviceAI #MachineLearning

Source: Introducing AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel: Open Models for Speech and Decisions on Apple Platforms

item.title: Meta unveils Muse Spark Open, runs on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios
item.description:
Meta unveils Muse Spark Open, runs on Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios

Meta announced the Muse Spark Open AI model today, calling it the “most capable US open-weight model to date.”

🔍 Overview

  • The company also says it’s the “first model in its class” that can “run on your desktop using two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios with the latest MLX framework.”
  • Meta and Apple, typically rivals, worked together on the launch and are publicly supporting each other.

🧩 How it works

  • The new model is a “natively multimodal model” with 816 billion total parameters.
  • It “excels at long‑horizon tasks, complex software engineering, and multi‑step reasoning.”
  • Apple’s MLX is described as an “array framework” for ML tasks on Apple Silicon and is used to run Muse Spark Open on the Mac Studios.

⚙️ Key details

  • Model name: Muse Spark Open
  • Weight release: Today (weights releasing today)
  • Hardware requirement: Two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios
  • Software framework: MLX (Apple’s array framework for ML on Apple Silicon)
  • Capabilities: Multimodal processing, long‑horizon reasoning, software‑engineering assistance, multi‑step reasoning

🚀 Availability

  • “Muse Spark Open – weights releasing today – runs great on new Mac Studios thanks to work with @johnternus and Apple,” Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said on X.
  • “Congrats to the team!” new Apple CEO John Ternus replied.

💡 Why it matters

  • Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang told Axios that the companies have been collaborating for several months, noting the partnership as a sign of “mommy and daddy playing nice again.”
  • Apple published a technical post about MLX, highlighting its role in enabling Muse Spark Open and two other open models on Apple Silicon.
Component Detail
Model Muse Spark Open
Parameter count 816 billion
Weight release Today
Required hardware Two Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios
Required software MLX framework

#Meta #Apple #MuseSpark #MLX #OnDeviceAI

Source: Meta and Apple team up to make Muse AI models run better on Macs

item.title: AI Edge Gallery Adds Support for Gemma 4 and On-Device Features
item.description:
AI Edge Gallery Adds Support for Gemma 4 and On-Device Features

AI Edge Gallery is a destination for running open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) directly on mobile hardware. The latest version introduces official support for the Gemma 4 family of models, enabling high-performance Generative AI to run fully offline and private.

🔍 Overview

All model inferences occur directly on the device hardware without requiring internet, which ensures privacy for images, prompts, and sensitive data. The platform utilizes Google AI Edge for core APIs and tools, along with LiteRT for optimized model execution.

⚙️ Key Details

Feature Description
Thinking Mode Allows users to see the model’s step-by-step reasoning process; currently supported by the Gemma 4 family.
Agent Skills Augments capabilities with tools such as interactive maps, Wikipedia for fact-grounding, and visual summary cards.
Multimodal Power Uses the photo gallery or camera to solve visual puzzles, identify objects, or generate detailed descriptions.
Voice Capabilities Real-time transcription and translation of voice recordings into text via on-device models.
Dedicated Workspace Provides granular control over model parameters like top-k and temperature for testing prompts and single-turn use cases.
Model Management Includes the ability to download models from a list, load custom models, and run benchmark tests on specific hardware.

🧩 Specialized Capabilities

Certain tasks are powered by a finetune of FunctionGemma 270m:

  • Offline device controls and automated tasks.
  • An experimental mini-game where natural language is used to harvest and plant a virtual garden.

Users can also load modular skills via GitHub Discussions community contributions or from a URL.

🚀 Availability

  • OS Requirements: Android 12 and up; iOS 17 and up.
  • Installation: Available via the App Store, Google Play, or as an apk from the latest release for users without Google Play access.

#AIEdgeGallery #Gemma4 #OnDeviceAI #LLM #MobileAI

Source: google-ai-edge/gallery

item.title: AI Edge Gallery adds support for Gemma 4 and Thinking Mode
item.description:
AI Edge Gallery adds support for Gemma 4 and Thinking Mode

The AI Edge Gallery has been updated to provide official support for the newly released Gemma 4 family of models, enabling users to run powerful open-source Large Language Models (LLMs) locally on mobile devices.

🔍 Overview

AI Edge Gallery is a flexible sandbox and destination for running open-source LLMs directly on hardware. All model inferences happen on-device, meaning no internet is required, ensuring privacy for prompts, images, and sensitive data.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Thinking Mode Allows users to see a model’s step-by-step reasoning process; currently works with supported models starting with Gemma 4.
Agent Skills Augments capabilities with tools like Wikipedia for fact-grounding, interactive maps, and visual summary cards.
Dedicated Workspace A space to test prompts and single-turn use cases with control over temperature and top-k parameters.
Model Management Allows users to download models from a list, load custom models, and run benchmark tests on specific hardware.

🧩 How it works

Users can access various on-device ML/GenAI use cases, including:

  • Multimodal Capabilities: Identifying objects, solving visual puzzles, or getting descriptions via the camera or photo gallery.
  • Audio Processing: Real-time transcription and translation of voice recordings into text.
  • Automated Tasks: Offline device controls and a virtual garden mini-game powered by a finetune of FunctionGemma 270m.
  • Modular Skills: Loading skills via URL or browsing community contributions on GitHub Discussions.

🚀 Availability

  • OS Requirements: Android 12 and up, and iOS 17 and up.
  • Installation: Available via Google Play, App Store, or as an apk from the latest release for users without Google Play access.
  • Technical Foundation: Powered by Google AI Edge (Core APIs and tools) and LiteRT (lightweight runtime for optimized execution).

#Gemma4 #AIEdgeGallery #OnDeviceAI #LLM #OpenSource

Source: google-ai-edge/gallery

item.title: 🎵 AI Sound Generation at Your Fingertips: Building a Real-Time Audio Creator on Arm CPUs
item.description:
🎵 AI Sound Generation at Your Fingertips: Building a Real-Time Audio Creator on Arm CPUs

Summary: Discover how a software engineer built a personal AI sound generator that creates unique audio samples in seconds—running entirely on Arm CPUs without cloud dependencies. This on-device solution integrates seamlessly with music production workflows, showing how efficient computing architectures can power creative AI tools locally.

🚀 From Imagination to Sound in Seconds

Have you ever been in the flow of creation when suddenly you need that perfect sound—but searching through libraries breaks your momentum? 𝗧𝗵𝗶𝘀 𝗶𝘀 𝘁𝗵𝗲 𝗽𝗿𝗼𝗯𝗹𝗲𝗺 I set out to solve as both a software engineer and music producer.

The result? A personal tool that generates unique, studio-ready sounds from simple text prompts—running 𝘤𝘰𝘮𝘱𝘭𝘦𝘵𝘦𝘭𝘺 on-device with an Arm-based CPU. No cloud services, no waiting, no interruptions to the creative process.

This isn’t just another AI demo. It’s a glimpse into how efficient computing architectures can transform creative workflows by bringing AI capabilities directly to the tools we already use.

🧠 The Technical Stack: Power Meets Efficiency

The magic behind this sound generator comes from combining several powerful technologies:

  • 🔊 Stable Audio Open model from Stability AI (via Hugging Face)
  • ⚙️ PyTorch and TorchAudio for the inference engine
  • 💻 Arm-based CPUs providing the computational muscle
  • 🎛️ Ableton Live integration for seamless creative handoff

What makes this approach different is that it runs 𝘄𝗶𝘁𝗵𝗼𝘂𝘁 dedicated GPUs or cloud connections, proving that today’s efficient CPUs can handle complex generative tasks when the pipeline is properly optimized.

🎹 Seamless Creative Integration

What truly makes this tool valuable is how it integrates into existing workflows. Instead of switching between applications or browser tabs, the generated sounds appear directly in Ableton Live’s browser.

Seconds later, that uniquely generated sound is ready to be dragged into a track, manipulated, and incorporated into a composition. No downloading files from cloud services, no copying between folders—just seamless creation.

The difference between this and other AI audio tools? 𝙏𝙝𝙚 𝙘𝙧𝙚𝙖𝙩𝙞𝙫𝙚 𝙛𝙡𝙤𝙬 𝙣𝙚𝙫𝙚𝙧 𝙨𝙩𝙤𝙥𝙨.

🔮 Why On-Device AI Matters for Creators

This project demonstrates something powerful about the future of creative tools:

  1. Flow preservation 🌊 - When AI runs locally, there’s no waiting that disrupts creativity

  2. Data privacy 🛡️ - Your creative prompts and outputs never leave your machine

  3. Ownership 🔐 - Complete control over your generated content

  4. Reliability ⚡ - No dependency on internet connections or cloud service availability

As Arm-based processors continue to evolve, we’ll see more AI workloads shifting from cloud to local execution. This isn’t just about technical efficiency—it’s about removing barriers between imagination and creation.

𝗧𝗵𝗲 𝗣𝗼𝘄𝗲𝗿 𝗼𝗳 𝗣𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗼𝗻𝗮𝗹𝗶𝘇𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻

Perhaps the most exciting aspect of this tool is that every generated sound is unique. The exact same prompt will produce different results each time, giving creators a sense of ownership over what they generate. This contrasts sharply with the sample packs and presets that lead to homogenized sounds across different artists’ work.

With on-device generation, you’re not just selecting from a menu—you’re describing what doesn’t yet exist and bringing it into being.

🌟 Looking Forward: Local AI as Creative Companion

While this project is a personal prototype, it points toward a future where AI becomes less of a remote service and more of an integrated creative companion. Imagine musical instruments with built-in sound generation, video editors with on-device visual effect creation, or design tools that generate textures and patterns in real-time.

The combination of efficient computing architectures like Arm and optimized AI models is making this future possible sooner than many expected. For developers and creators alike, this opens new possibilities for tools that enhance rather than interrupt the creative process.

What would your creative workflow look like if you could generate exactly what you imagine, right when you need it, without leaving your primary creative environment?
